caption: The drawing depicts a single tool positioned vertically in the center of the image, with its handle at the top and the working end at the bottom. The tool appears to be a wooden-handled auger or chisel with a horizontal crossbar handle. The main central shaft of the tool is cylindrical and made of a medium brown wood, showing the grain and some wear, with detailed shading to indicate its three-dimensional shape. The top of the tool has a rounded, disc-like end cap. The crossbar handle pierces horizontally through the upper section of the tool's body and is also made of wood, colored a slightly lighter brown than the central shaft, and ends in rounded knobs on each side. Below the handle, the central shaft tapers and then expands before transitioning into a metal section. The metal portion is straight with a flat chisel-like blade at the bottom, rendered in grayish-brown metal tones, and the tip of the blade has a slight curvature and a pointed screw-like end. The background of the drawing is an off-white or pale beige color with no additional objects or patterns. The artist's signature "MICHAEL CHOMYK" is visible in small, neat printed letters in the lower right corner.
title: Bishop Hill: Auger
